name: Learn: Pod & Container Security
objective: CKS › Minimize Microservice Vulnerabilities. Drill EVERY pod-hardening corner harder than the exam: runAsNonRoot/runAsUser, drop-ALL capabilities, readOnlyRootFilesystem, seccomp RuntimeDefault, privilege-escalation lockdown, a fully restricted-compliant pod, Pod Security Admission (enforce + audit/warn, pinned), and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.
description: Eight strict hardening practicals across securityContext and Pod Security Admission. Each Check shows which requirements you met and the exact reason for any you missed.

questions.title: Run as a non-root UID
questions.teach:
Containers run as **root (UID 0)** unless told otherwise. In the container `securityContext`, `runAsNonRoot: true` makes the kubelet refuse any image resolving to UID 0, and `runAsUser: <uid>` pins a specific non-zero UID.

**Gotcha:** `runAsNonRoot: true` alone won't start a root image like busybox — you must also pin a non-zero `runAsUser`.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `cks-podsec`, create pod `secure-app` (image `busybox:1.36`, container `app`, command `sleep 3600`) whose container `securityContext` sets `runAsNonRoot: true` and `runAsUser: 1000`.

Target: container reports `runAsNonRoot=true` and `runAsUser=1000`.
questions.hint: Write YAML with `spec.containers[0].securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true` and `runAsUser: 1000`, then `kubectl apply -f -`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: secure-app, namespace: cks-podsec }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      runAsUser: 1000
YAML

questions.title: Drop ALL capabilities, add one back
questions.teach:
Linux **capabilities** slice up root's powers. The hardening pattern is drop everything, then add back only what's needed, under the container `securityContext`: `capabilities: { drop: [ALL], add: [NET_BIND_SERVICE] }`.

**Gotcha:** write names **without** the `CAP_` prefix — `NET_BIND_SERVICE`, not `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`.
questions.prompt:
Create pod `cap-app` in `cks-podsec` (image `busybox:1.36`, container `app`, `sleep 3600`, `runAsUser: 1000`) that **drops ALL** capabilities and **adds** only `NET_BIND_SERVICE`.

Target: `capabilities.drop=[ALL]` and `capabilities.add=[NET_BIND_SERVICE]` exactly.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: cap-app, namespace: cks-podsec }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    securityContext:
      runAsUser: 1000
      capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"], add: ["NET_BIND_SERVICE"] }
YAML

questions.title: Read-only root filesystem + writable scratch
questions.teach:
`readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` (container-level) makes `/` immutable so an attacker can't drop binaries. Apps that still need scratch space get a writable volume mounted at just those paths, e.g. an `emptyDir` at `/tmp`.

**Gotcha:** without a writable mount an app that writes temp files crashes (`CrashLoopBackOff`).
questions.prompt:
Create pod `ro-app` in `cks-podsec` (image `busybox:1.36`, container `app`, `sleep 3600`, `runAsUser: 1000`) with `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` plus an `emptyDir` volume mounted at `/tmp`.

Target: container `readOnlyRootFilesystem=true` and a `/tmp` volumeMount backed by an emptyDir.
questions.hint: Container `securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`; add `volumes: [{name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}]` and `volumeMounts: [{name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: ro-app, namespace: cks-podsec }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    securityContext:
      runAsUser: 1000
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
    volumeMounts: [ { name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp } ]
  volumes: [ { name: tmp, emptyDir: {} } ]
YAML

questions.title: seccomp RuntimeDefault
questions.teach:
**seccomp** filters which syscalls a container may make; containers run **Unconfined** by default. `seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault` applies the runtime's built-in profile — the file-free way the *restricted* standard wants. It can sit at pod or container level.

**Gotcha:** `type` is **case-sensitive** — `RuntimeDefault`, not `runtimedefault`.
questions.prompt:
Create pod `seccomp-app` in `cks-podsec` (image `busybox:1.36`, container `app`, `sleep 3600`, `runAsUser: 1000`) with a **pod-level** `seccompProfile` of type `RuntimeDefault`.

Target: `spec.securityContext.seccompProfile.type=RuntimeDefault`.
questions.hint: Add `securityContext: { seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault } }` at the pod `spec` level.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: seccomp-app, namespace: cks-podsec }
spec:
  securityContext:
    seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault }
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    securityContext:
      runAsUser: 1000
YAML

questions.title: Block privilege escalation
questions.teach:
`allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` (container-level) stops a process gaining more privileges than its parent (blocks setuid/setgid escalation), and `privileged: false` keeps the container out of privileged mode. Both belong in the container `securityContext`.

**Gotcha:** `allowPrivilegeEscalation` defaults to **true** when a container runs privileged or has `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` — set it explicitly to `false`.
questions.prompt:
Create pod `noesc-app` in `cks-podsec` (image `busybox:1.36`, container `app`, `sleep 3600`, `runAsUser: 1000`) whose container `securityContext` sets `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` and `privileged: false`.

Target: container `allowPrivilegeEscalation=false` and `privileged=false`.
questions.hint: Under the container `securityContext`: `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` and `privileged: false`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: noesc-app, namespace: cks-podsec }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    securityContext:
      runAsUser: 1000
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      privileged: false
YAML

questions.title: A fully restricted-compliant pod
questions.teach:
The *restricted* Pod Security Standard wants **all** of: `runAsNonRoot: true`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, `capabilities.drop: [ALL]`, and `seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault`. Combine them so the pod would pass under `enforce=restricted`.

**Gotcha:** restricted requires `capabilities.drop` contain **ALL** (not just a few caps) and forbids adding anything except `NET_BIND_SERVICE`.
questions.prompt:
Create pod `restricted-app` in `cks-podsec` (image `busybox:1.36`, container `app`, `sleep 3600`) that satisfies the *restricted* standard:
- pod-level `runAsNonRoot: true`, `seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault`
- container `runAsUser: 1000`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, `capabilities.drop: [ALL]`

Target: every field above is set as specified.
questions.hint: Put `runAsNonRoot` + `seccompProfile` under `spec.securityContext`; put `runAsUser`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, and `capabilities.drop:[ALL]` under the container `securityContext`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: restricted-app, namespace: cks-podsec }
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault }
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    securityContext:
      runAsUser: 1000
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
YAML

questions.title: Pod Security Admission: enforce + audit, pinned
questions.teach:
**Pod Security Admission** applies a Pod Security Standard per namespace via labels. `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=<level>` rejects violating pods; `audit`/`warn` only log/warn. Pin each mode with its `*-version` label so policy won't drift on upgrade.

**Gotcha:** `enforce` only checks pods at create/update — it does **not** evict pods already running.
questions.prompt:
Label namespace `cks-locked` to **enforce** `restricted` pinned to `v1.30`, and additionally **audit** at `baseline` pinned to `v1.30`.

Target: labels `enforce=restricted`, `enforce-version=v1.30`, `audit=baseline`, `audit-version=v1.30`.

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a pod that won't start
questions.teach:
A pod that fails `runAsNonRoot` sits in a non-Ready state; `kubectl describe pod

` Events show `container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root` — the container set `runAsNonRoot: true` but no non-zero `runAsUser`, so the root image is rejected. Pin a non-zero `runAsUser`. **Gotcha:** fix the **securityContext** (add a non-zero `runAsUser`), not the image — a pod spec is immutable, so delete-and-recreate the pod with the fix.
questions.prompt:
Pod `broken-app` in `cks-podsec` **never becomes Ready** — `kubectl -n cks-podsec get pod broken-app` shows it isn't running. Diagnose the securityContext fault and fix it so the pod runs as a non-root UID.

Target: a pod named `broken-app` is `Running` with `runAsNonRoot=true` and a non-zero `runAsUser`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n cks-podsec describe pod broken-app` → 'container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root'. It sets `runAsNonRoot: true` but no `runAsUser`. Delete it and recreate with `runAsUser: 1000` added.
questions.solution:
# describe shows: container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root (0)
kubectl -n cks-podsec delete pod broken-app --force --grace-period=0
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: broken-app, namespace: cks-podsec }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      runAsUser: 1000
YAML

verification.description: broken-app Running with runAsNonRoot + non-zero runAsUser
